title: Patient, parent and clinician voices – establishing national and international research priorities for paediatric anaesthesia and perioperative medicine
summary: This study aims to identify which topics related to anaesthesia, pain management and perioperative care in children should be prioritised for future research. Children and young people, parents/carers and healthcare professionals will participate in anonymous online surveys and share their ideas and priorities. The results will be used to create national and international top-10 lists of research priorities in paediatric anaesthesia and perioperative medicine. The goal is to support future research that is more closely aligned with the needs and experiences of children and families.
conditions: Children (6-18 years), Parents and Carers, Clinicians

interventions.name:
Children (6-18 years)
Children and young people aged 6–18 years providing research ideas and priorities for paediatric anaesthesia and perioperative medicine via an anonymous online survey.

Parents and Carers
Parents, legal guardians or carers providing research ideas and priorities for paediatric anaesthesia and perioperative care in children via an anonymous online survey.

Clinicians
Physicians, nurses and other healthcare professionals  providing research ideas and priorities for paediatric anaesthesia and perioperative care via an anonymous online survey.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Children and young people aged 6–18 years, parents/carers regardless of previous surgery or anaesthesia experience, and clinicians working in paediatric perioperative medicine will be included. Participants must live in Germany at the time of participation.
Exclusion criteria:
Participants who do not reside in Germany at the time of participation will be excluded from the German cohort. Participants will indicate their place of residence (country/state). If participants indicate residence in Switzerland or Austria, their data may be included in the international as well as Swiss or Austrian cohorts, but will not be included in analyses of the German cohort.
